implementation: M5 library seam: backend session64 authorizes own Player through bounded worker; separate CSPRNG128bit launch32, one-use login, explicit redirect-delivery handoff, one channel generation with repeated backend authorization. No listener/config/runtime behavior change.

reuse.direct: CP236 SQLite/Argon2id/session/Player/schema2; CP243 worker Pending/cancel; CP244 idleTTL/rate. CP214–217 token/count1/channel typed layout and existing kr-wire::crypt; CP225 network suffix. No new DB, KDF, wire algorithm, VN port or SDK RE.
reuse.sources: local/research/codex/rust-m5-bridge-source-r1/reuse.json; oracle.json verifies 3 CP217 complete raw pins against native input hashes/name-ID-echo, not generated encoder outputs.
reuse.avoided: No repeat M4 Free startup, native error parser, full codec/provider/general client RE.

criteria.criterion: Backend strong session/own player checked at issue/login/channel; two accounts sharing one IP are distinct; source IP alone grants no ownership.
Frontend32 distinct from backend64; hash-only lookup; one use, delivered redirect required, name/ID/echo/peer checks; lifetime and generation fences.
No mutex during DB await; queued cancellation, Busy/Closed, expired work and old-generation drops cannot publish/erase a newer owner.
Execution-time UTC rejects session expired during queue; revoke/rename/real SQLite write fault fail closed; failed channel check removes its generation.
Offline decoder matches unchanged CP217 login positive/bad-token inputs and channel name/ID/echo; malformed/count/size/peer/optional flag guards.

failures_and_corrections: Initial compile errors (MutexGuard coercion and wrong rename API/argument order) retained before acceptance.

Preliminary queue cancellation test resumed the worker and immediately assumed the canceled queue slot had drained. Backend correctly returned Busy; test fixed with a deterministic barrier, failures retained. No queue timeout or capacity increase.

R1 acceptance passed 7 tests/6 DBs, but manual source review found the optional-string flag was not constrained. R2 explicitly requires off at name+31, preserves 23 opaque bytes, adds negative control. R1 raw/source retained; no changes during either frozen run.
limits: Library seam only. Existing diagnostic service listener/config/packet logging/room behavior unchanged; kr-service rebuilt but not natively certified for M5.
Three old native bodies replayed offline are not a fresh KR end-to-end run on Rust account backend; two implementations agreeing is not a native authentication oracle.

Field36 echo32 and peer IPv4 remain legacy correlators/profile fences, not strong channel credentials. Opaque16 and other23 C2S6 trailing bytes are not interpreted as secrets. No original server auth or encrypted transport claim.

Only count1/token32/body61 and channel name5/name7/count1/optional-off. Backend names3..15 do not automatically all project to KR. Dynamic account profile writer and listener integration still missing.

Process-local capacity1..32, original launch TTL1ms..10s, echo budget1024/no reuse until process exit. No durable restart/multi-process replay fence; check launch startup timing before serving integration. Expired pending entries swept on new admission, bound entries require check/drop by serving caller.

Worker current UTC is sampled when DB work executes; authorization is a transaction-time check, not continuous revocation. Serving must select authorization boundaries and invalidate room/UDP/queued work on failure; no socket integration or periodic check has been implemented.

Backend session is borrowed, never created by this bridge; cancellation only removes bridge generation and zeroizes copies, does not revoke a caller-owned session. Backend idle renewal occurs on each successful own-player authorization including a canceled operation that was already running.

No launcher/admin web API, native password UI, frontend error-reply adaptation, account resume/match restore, ban UI, multiroom, result-reward durability, load or backup/restore acceptance. M5 remains partial and M4 Free remains blocked; Internet thật chưa kiểm.
